newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo rivals prolong truce for one week.
newsitem.headline: Congo rivals prolong truce for one week.

text.p: The warring factions in the Congo Republic capital Brazzaville agreed on Friday to extend a 72-hour truce for a further seven days, a spokesman for Brazzaville mayor and mediator Bernard Kolelas said.
The previous ceasefire had been due to expire at midnight local time (2300 GMT) on Friday.
"The chiefs of staff of both sides have agreed to prolong the ceasefire for a period of seven days starting tonight at midnight," the spokesman told Reuters in Kinshasa by telephone from Brazzaville.

He was reading from a statement signed on behalf of supporters of President Pascal Lissouba, his rival former military president Denis Sassou Nguesso and Kolelas, whose own forces have so far kept out of any fighting.

All three men had been due to contest a presidential election on July 27. Bloody ethnic and political clashes, which have killed hundreds of people if not more, have made parts of the capital of the oil-producing former French colony no-go areas.
Fighting broke out on June 5 after governmment soldiers surrounded the home of Sassou Nguesso as part of a crackdown on private militias and illegally held weapons in the run-up to the poll.
